description:
## Why

Project stance (decided 2026-05-11): the workspace ships standards-based **mechanisms** for implementing, testing, enforcing, and linting PKI policy. It does NOT ship canonical encodings of any single organization's policy — CA/B Forum, DoD, Mozilla / Apple / Microsoft root programs, or individual CA CPSs.

Today, `pkix-profiles` ships `TlsBrProfile` and a CA/B-Forum-flavoured `SmimeProfile` (Mailbox-validated / strict tier with SC-081 validity caps). `pkix-lint` ships `cabf.br.tls` lint bundles. Both blur the line between framework and policy.

Realign: framework + RFC-baseline content stays in the main crates. CA/B Forum specifics move to sibling reference crates (`pkix-profiles-cabf`, `pkix-lint-cabf`) clearly marked as 'reference / not authoritative — fork and adapt to your deployment's current CA/B Forum interpretation.'

## The line

**Stays in `pkix-profiles` / `pkix-lint`** (standards bodies / universal industry consensus):

- The `Profile` trait, `ValidationPolicy` struct, framework helpers.
- The `Lint` trait, `LintRunner`, `Finding`, `EvaluationReport`, `DeviationStore`.
- `BasicSmimeProfile` — RFC 8551 §3 cert-profile baseline (id-kp-emailProtection EKU + rfc822Name SAN). Mailbox-binding logic, no validity caps, no key-size floors, no identity-tier policy OIDs.
- `BasicTlsProfile` — RFC 5280 + RFC 6125 server identity verification + universally-required id-kp-serverAuth EKU. No validity caps, no key-size floors.
- RFC-conformance lints (RFC 5280, RFC 6960, RFC 4518, etc.). Standards-body content.

**Moves to `pkix-profiles-cabf`** (CA/B Forum-specific reference):

- `TlsBrProfile` and SC-081 validity caps.
- `SmimeProfile` Mailbox-validated / strict, Organization-validated, Sponsor-validated, Individual-validated tiers (PKIX-jbvb scope reparents here).
- CA/B Forum policy OIDs and per-tier required-field tables.

**Moves to `pkix-lint-cabf`** (CA/B Forum-specific reference):

- `cabf.br.tls` / `cabf.br.smime` lint bundles.
- Anything keyed off a CA/B Forum ballot number (SC-081, etc.).

## Acceptance

- [ ] AGENTS.md encodes the framework-not-policy stance as a non-negotiable.
- [ ] `pkix-profiles-cabf` exists as a workspace crate, depending on `pkix-profiles` framework.
- [ ] `pkix-lint-cabf` exists as a workspace crate, depending on `pkix-lint` framework.
- [ ] Both new crates carry a prominent rustdoc + README header: 'Reference implementation of CA/B Forum requirements — not authoritative. Fork and adapt to your deployment's current CA/B Forum interpretation. See https://cabforum.org/ for the current Baseline Requirements text.'
- [ ] `pkix-profiles` keeps `BasicSmimeProfile` + `BasicTlsProfile` as RFC-baseline references.
- [ ] `pkix-lint` keeps only RFC-conformance lints.
- [ ] PKIX-jbvb (S/MIME BR sub-profile families) reparented to `pkix-profiles-cabf` scope, with the reference-not-authoritative framing baked into its acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Top-level README + CHANGELOG migration notes for downstream consumers.

## Out of scope

- Maintaining `pkix-profiles-cabf` / `pkix-lint-cabf` long-term — Mark or another maintainer commits to keeping them current with CA/B Forum ballots; they may also choose to move them out of the workspace later.
- Encoding DoD / federal PKI policies (out-of-tree concern entirely).
- Encoding individual root-program policies (Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft) — out-of-tree.

## Children

- `.1` AGENTS.md stance update (anchor)
- `.2` Create `pkix-profiles-cabf` crate
- `.3` Create `pkix-lint-cabf` crate
- `.4` Refactor `pkix-profiles` to framework + BasicSmime + BasicTls
- `.5` Refactor `pkix-lint` to framework + RFC-conformance lints
- `.6` Reparent PKIX-jbvb to pkix-profiles-cabf
- `.7` README + CHANGELOG migration docs

title: Realign pkix-profiles + pkix-lint: framework + RFC-baseline in main crates, CA/B Forum policy in -cabf reference crates
